body:
## Summary
- stop revoking Camera from inside the instrumentation process, which Android 16 terminates with SIGKILL
- add a serial-scoped Make target that performs permission and package cleanup only after instrumentation exits
- fail closed when the app or test package is already installed, preserving existing app data
- add a JVM contract preventing in-process revocation and unsafe cleanup regressions

## Verification
- `make baseline-android-camera-recovery-device-test ANDROID_CAMERA_RECOVERY_SERIAL=<redacted-adb-serial>`: 1/1 passed on Nubia P0110/pacific Android 16
- post-run: app/test packages absent, Camera app-op has no UID, adb reverse empty, no TCP 54321 listener
- preinstalled-app safety probe: target exits 2 and leaves the installed app present
- `make baseline-android-check`
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest tests.phase3.test_repository_privacy -v`

## Scope
No macOS Host was started and no macOS Screen Recording, Accessibility, or Microphone permission was requested. This fixes the Android test lifecycle; it does not close any Host-backed Phase 0 gate.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added an opt-in Android camera-permission recovery device test with explicit device selection.
  * Added safeguards to avoid replacing existing app or test packages.
  * Added automatic cleanup after successful or failed test runs.
  * Improved package checks so device-query failures are reported instead of hidden.

* **Tests**
  * Added validation covering host-side permission revocation, serial-scoped execution, package preservation, and cleanup behavior.

title: fix(android): clean up camera recovery tests after instrumentation
